weeks.title: Course Introduction and Relational Structure
weeks.summary: Course expectations; relations, tuples, attributes, domains, schemas, and relation instances.
activities: Identify relations, attributes, tuples, domains, schemas, and instances in the course-registration example.
Confirm that the lab runner can list the available chapters.
evidence: A schema identification sheet.
A key map with reasons based on stated business rules.
weeks.next: Week 2 applies keys, schema diagrams, and relational-algebra operations.

weeks.title: Keys and Relational Algebra
weeks.summary: Primary, candidate, composite, and foreign keys; schema diagrams; selection, projection, product, join, and set operations.

readings.label: Chapter 2, Sections 5-6, Common Errors, and Summary

activities: Predict each small relation before executing the corresponding SQL example.
Compare the predicted and observed results and correct one misconception.
evidence: Key and foreign-key decisions with reasons.
Intermediate and final relational-algebra results.
One corrected misconception.
weeks.next: Week 3 expresses relational operations with introductory SQL.

weeks.title: Basic SQL
weeks.summary: DDL basics; SELECT, FROM, WHERE, aliases, expressions, duplicates, patterns, ordering, and SQL set operations.
activities: Use the Chapter 3 SQL file through Example 8 and predict rows, columns, duplicates, and order before execution.
Keep the complete automated chapter run for Week 4 after the remaining Chapter 3 topics are introduced.
evidence: SQL statements and predictions for selected basic queries.
Checked rows, columns, duplicates, and display order.
weeks.next: Week 4 adds NULL, grouping, selected subqueries, and reversible modifications.

weeks.title: NULL, Aggregation, and Selected Subqueries
weeks.summary: Three-valued logic, aggregation, GROUP BY, HAVING, selected subqueries, common table expressions, and reversible data modification.

readings.label: Chapter 3, Sections 5-8, Common Errors, and Summary

activities: Predict the effect of NULL before running each relevant query.
Verify grouped and nested queries from the inside out.
Run the complete Chapter 3 lab after studying all selected sections.
evidence: One NULL prediction and correction.
One grouped query with each filtering stage identified.
One subquery with checked intermediate and final results.
weeks.next: Week 5 uses explicit joins, views, constraints, and transaction boundaries.

weeks.title: Intermediate SQL
weeks.summary: Explicit joins, outer joins, ON and WHERE, views, integrity constraints, reference actions, and basic transactions.
activities: Compare inner- and outer-join results before moving a predicate.
Test one valid and one invalid constraint case.
Verify rollback and commit behavior.
evidence: Join predictions and checked results.
Constraint success and failure evidence.
Transaction states before and after rollback.
weeks.next: Week 6 is Written Exam 1 on the selected Chapter 2-4 material.

weeks.title: Written Exam 1
weeks.summary: Written Exam 1 covers the selected classroom material from Chapters 2-4.
activities: Complete the individual examination under the announced rules.
After feedback is released, correct one representative error using new data.
evidence: The submitted examination.
The assigned correction record after feedback.
weeks.next: Week 7 introduces selected advanced SQL features.

weeks.title: Selected Advanced SQL
weeks.summary: Ranking and window functions, recursive CTEs, one row-level audit trigger, and the purpose and interface of stored routines.
activities: Trace recursion by round and explain its termination condition.
Predict ranking results when ties occur.
Check the trigger event, condition, action, and audit result.
evidence: Recursive rounds and termination explanation.
Predicted and observed ranking results.
Trigger before-and-after evidence.
weeks.next: Week 8 begins conceptual database design with the E-R model.

weeks.title: E-R Design Foundations
weeks.summary: Requirements, entities, attributes, relationships, roles, cardinality, participation, keys, and weak entities.
activities: Derive an initial E-R diagram from the supplied course-registration rules.
Annotate each cardinality, participation, and key decision with requirement evidence.
evidence: An initial E-R diagram.
Requirement-based reasons for the main design decisions.
weeks.next: Week 9 contains asynchronous review while the instructor attends INFORMS.

weeks.title: Asynchronous Review
weeks.summary: No class, examination, or new material is scheduled because the instructor is attending INFORMS.
activities: Rework one SQL question and check one core Chapter 2-5 judgment.
Record the original answer, checking evidence, and correction.
commands: py -3 resources/run_labs.py ch02 ch03 ch04 ch05
evidence: One asynchronous review record containing a prediction, check, and correction.
weeks.next: Week 10 completes E-R design and maps the design to relations.

weeks.title: E-R Design and Relational Mapping
weeks.summary: Redundancy, design choices, E-R-to-relational mapping, keys, foreign keys, and mapped-schema verification.

readings.label: Chapter 6, Sections 7-10, Common Errors, and Summary

activities: Check an E-R diagram against the stated business rules.
Map the revised design to relations and test the mapped schema.
evidence: A revised E-R diagram.
Mapped relations, primary keys, and foreign keys.
Predicted and observed schema tests.
weeks.next: Week 11 evaluates relational designs with normalization concepts.

weeks.title: Normalization
weeks.summary: Anomalies, functional dependencies, attribute closure, lossless decomposition, spurious tuples, and introductory 3NF and BCNF decisions.
activities: Identify repeated facts and modification anomalies.
Calculate one attribute closure and test one decomposition.
Compare predicted and observed reconstruction results.
evidence: A functional-dependency table with business-rule support.
Closure steps and candidate-key reasoning.
Lossless and deliberately lossy reconstruction evidence.
weeks.next: Week 12 is Written Exam 2 on the selected Chapter 5-7 material.

weeks.title: Written Exam 2
weeks.summary: Written Exam 2 covers the selected classroom material from Chapters 5-7.
activities: Complete the individual examination under the announced rules.
After feedback is released, correct one assigned SQL, mapping, or normalization error.
evidence: The submitted examination.
The assigned correction record after feedback.
weeks.next: Week 13 begins physical database topics with indexing.

weeks.title: Indexing
weeks.summary: Index purpose, B+ tree equality and range access, composite-column order, covering indexes, and query-plan evidence.
activities: Predict an access path before creating an index.
Compare the plans before and after the index and state a bounded conclusion.
evidence: A query-to-index reason.
Before-and-after plans.
One write or storage cost not measured by the plan output.
weeks.next: Week 14 places index access inside query processing and optimization.

weeks.title: Query Processing and Optimization
weeks.summary: Scans and searches, join access order, result-equivalence checks, basic selectivity, catalog statistics, ANALYZE, and conservative plan interpretation.
activities: Check result equivalence before comparing plans.
Inspect SCAN, SEARCH, access order, statistics, and omitted execution evidence.
Evaluate one proposed index or rewrite without overclaiming.
evidence: Original and comparison SQL with equivalence evidence.
Statistics and both query plans.
One supported conclusion and one unsupported conclusion.
weeks.next: Week 15 moves from individual query plans to transactions and schedules.

weeks.title: Transactions
weeks.summary: Transaction boundaries, ACID, transaction states, schedules, conflicts, precedence graphs, recoverability, and isolation phenomena.
activities: Predict rollback and commit results before running the SQL activity.
Build a precedence graph and evaluate serializability and recoverability separately.
evidence: Before-and-after transaction states.
One acyclic and one cyclic precedence graph.
Separate recoverability and isolation decisions with model limitations.
weeks.next: Week 16 connects transaction requirements to locks, deadlock, logs, and recovery.

weeks.title: Concurrency Control, Recovery, and Review
weeks.summary: S/X lock compatibility, grant and wait decisions, wait-for graphs, deadlock, log old and new values, write-ahead logging, and one simplified redo and undo case.
activities: Complete S/X compatibility and grant-or-wait decisions.
Build a wait-for graph and identify a cycle.
Use transaction status and log values to complete one redo and undo analysis.
evidence: Lock decisions and a wait-for graph.
A simplified recovery table with redo and undo reasons.
A review record connecting indexes, plans, transactions, and recovery.
weeks.next: Week 17 is the university anniversary make-up holiday with no scheduled class.

weeks.title: University Anniversary Make-Up Holiday
weeks.summary: No class, examination, assignment, or new material is scheduled because of the university anniversary make-up holiday.
activities: No required course activity is scheduled.
weeks.next: Week 18 is Written Exam 3 during the official final-examination week.

weeks.title: Written Exam 3
weeks.summary: Written Exam 3 covers the selected Chapter 14-19 material and cumulative application of previously taught SQL and database-design concepts.
activities: Complete the individual final examination under the announced rules.
evidence: The submitted examination.
weeks.next: The course concludes after the final examination and any officially arranged make-up assessment.
